note: Each sample invokes candidate-headroom-large.mjs in a fresh process with --runs=1. Partial rows and projection rows are not full StAX parity rows.

childSourceContract.parserInput: Rows use StreamReaderSync over a synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> generated by byteBatches(fixture).
childSourceContract.arrayBufferConsumption: The generated row cycle is encoded into Uint8Array fixtures; measured rows consume synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> parser pulls, not a pure ReadableStream and not one full 1 GiB ArrayBuffer parser input.
childSourceContract.batchBackpressure: byteBatches(fixture) yields one grouped Uint8Array[] batch per synchronous parser pull and does not prebuild the repeated 1 GiB+ stream.
childSourceContract.multiChunkBatchCost: The current sync cursor can use a single Uint8Array batch item as a view, but a batch containing multiple Uint8Array chunks is concatenated into one parser buffer before scanning.
childSourceContract.readableStreamScope: This Node/Bun large matrix does not consume a pure ReadableStream directly; browser fetch streaming rows are measured in browser-candidate-headroom.
childSourceContract.corpusScope: generated fixtures prepare one row cycle before timing and replay that cycle as byte batches to the target size.

sourceContract.multiChunkBatchCost: Each child process invokes candidate-headroom-large.mjs. With the current sync cursor, batchSize=1 can scan a single Uint8Array view, while batchSize>1 groups chunks and triggers multi-chunk concatenation before parser scanning.

findings.summary: Each sample was measured by a separate runtime process, unlike same-process runs-based timing stability.
Projection rows are reported as selected-field projected records and are not full StAX event-parity rows.
Partial stream rows report selected parser work and are not full StAX event-parity rows.
No full-string row reported a 200 MiB/s bounded-memory counterexample in these independent process samples.
